criteria.justification: The response immediately makes a clear call to “roll back—or feature-flag off—the new integration” and restore the last known-good behavior.

It explicitly identifies rollback as reversible because the launch can be restored after testing, while noting that continued incorrect signals may trigger customer actions that cannot easily be undone; it also rejects an inadequately tested expedited fix.

The response directly weighs the public commitment against accumulating hourly harm, concluding that launch momentum does not outweigh incorrect production risk signals, support burden, and reputational damage.
It explicitly says to “avoid attempting an expedited, inadequately tested code fix in production” and instead calls for the properly scoped fix to be implemented and validated over several days.

It provides detailed follow-through: validate recovery, remediate already-generated alerts, communicate with customers and stakeholders, add regression and canary testing, and relaunch only after validation and incident review.
